## 4. Prepare GWAS summary statistics

### 4.1 Define a helper function `prep_gemma_zscores()`

```{r}
#| label: helper-function-prep-gemma-zscores

#' Prepare GEMMA GWAS z-scores
#' 
#' Calculate a Wald-style z-score (Beta / SE) for each SNP-trait 
#' association and keep the columns needed for downstream analysis.
#'
#' @param gemma_dt A data frame or data.table containing SNP_ID, Trait, Beta, and SE columns.
#' @return  A data.table with columns id, Trait, Beta, SE, and z.
#'   Rows with missing z-scores are removed.
prep_gemma_zscores <- function(gemma_dt){
  gwas_dt <- copy(as.data.table(gemma_dt))
  gwas_dt[, z := Beta / SE]
  
  gwas_dt[
    , 
    .(
      id = SNP_ID, 
      Trait = Trait,
      Beta = Beta,
      SE = SE,
      z = z
    )
  ][!is.na(z)]
}
```

### 4.2 Inspect the resulting z-scores

```{r}
#| label: inspect-zscores

gwas_zscore <- prep_gemma_zscores(gemma_gwas_dt)

head(gwas_zscore, 10)
```

**Observations**

The GEMMA results were reduced to SNP ID, trait, effect estimate, standard error, and z-score. The z-score preserves the direction of the estimated effect and expresses its size relative to its standard error. The first ten rows include both positive and negative associations.

## 5. Define the locus fine-mapping function

### 5.1 Define helpers for the locus fine-mapping function

```{r}
#| label: helper-select-locus-genotypes

#' Select genotype rows within a genomic window
#' 
#' @param geno_dt Genotype data.table with SNP identifiers in the SNP column.
#' @param chr Chromosome identifier.
#' @param start_pos,end_pos Inclusive genomic window boundaries.
#' @return A data.table of SNPs in the window, with an added pos column.
select_locus_genotypes <- function(
    geno_dt, chr, start_pos, end_pos
){
  locus_dt <- geno_dt[grepl(paste0("^0?", chr, ":"), SNP)]
  locus_dt[, pos := as.numeric(tstrsplit(SNP, ":")[[2]])]
  locus_dt[pos >= start_pos & pos <= end_pos]
}
```

```{r}
#| label: helper-align-locus-samples

#' Align genotype rows with expression samples
#'
#' Match complete sample IDs and construct a sample-by-SNP matrix.
#'
#' @param locus_geno_dt Genotype rows selected for one locus.
#' @param geno_dt Full genotype table.
#' @param expr_dt Expression table with gene IDs in the ID column.
#' @return A list containing X, expr_cols, and idx_expr; NULL if fewer
#'   than two matching samples or variable SNPs remain.
align_locus_samples <- function(locus_geno_dt, geno_dt, expr_dt) {
  expr_cols <- setdiff(names(expr_dt), "ID")
  geno_cols <- setdiff(names(geno_dt), c("SNP", "pos"))
  
  if (anyDuplicated(expr_cols) || anyDuplicated(geno_cols)) {
    stop("Sample column names must be unique.")
  }
  
  common_samples <- expr_cols[expr_cols %in% geno_cols]
  
  if (length(common_samples) < 2) {
    message("Fewer than two matching expression/genotype samples.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  idx_expr <- match(common_samples, expr_cols)
  idx_geno <- match(common_samples, geno_cols)
  
  X <- t(as.matrix(locus_geno_dt[, ..geno_cols]))[
    idx_geno, , drop = FALSE
  ]
  colnames(X) <- locus_geno_dt$SNP
  
  snp_variance <- apply(X, 2, var, na.rm = TRUE)
  X <- X[, is.finite(snp_variance) & snp_variance > 0, drop = FALSE]
  
  if (ncol(X) < 2) {
    message("Fewer than two variable SNPs remain.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  list(X = X, expr_cols = expr_cols, idx_expr = idx_expr)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: helper-build-gene-entry

#' Construct a gene's predicted-expression signal
#'
#' Fit a separate expression-on-genotype regression for each SNP.
#' Combine its weights with GWAS z-scores and the locus LD matrix
#' to obtain one gene-level pseudo-SNP signal.
#'
#' @param gene Candidate gene ID.
#' @param expr_dt Expression data.table with IDs in the ID column.
#' @param aligned Output from align_locus_samples().
#' @param ld_snps SNP correlation matrix for the locus.
#' @param z_sub GWAS z-score rows for the selected trait.
#' @return A list containing the SNP IDs, gene z-score, and
#'   gene–SNP correlations; NULL if this gene cannot be modeled.
build_gene_entry <- function(
    gene, expr_dt, aligned, ld_snps, z_sub
) {
  gene_row <- expr_dt[ID %in% gene]
  
  if (nrow(gene_row) == 0){
    message(sprintf(" [skip] %s not found in expression matrix.", gene))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  expr_cols <- aligned$expr_cols
  y <- as.numeric(
    unlist(gene_row[1, ..expr_cols], use.names = FALSE)
  )[aligned$idx_expr]
  
  valid <- complete.cases(y, aligned$X)
  X_gene <- aligned$X[valid, , drop = FALSE]
  y_gene <- y[valid]
  
  
  if (ncol(X_gene) < 2){
    message(sprintf(" [skip] %s: too few complete samples.", gene))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  snp_variance <- apply(X_gene, 2, var, na.rm = TRUE)
  X_gene <- X_gene[
    ,
    !is.na(snp_variance) & snp_variance > 0,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  
  if (ncol(X_gene) < 2){
    message(sprintf(" [skip] %s: fewer than two variable SNPs.", gene))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  weights <- apply(
    X_gene, 2,
    function(snp) coef(lm(y_gene ~ snp))[2]
  )
  weights[is.na(weights)] <- 0
  
  common_snps <- intersect(colnames(X_gene), z_sub$id)
  
  if (length(common_snps) < 2){
    message(sprintf(" [skip] %s: fewer than two SNPs overlap GWAS.", gene))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  ld_gene <- ld_snps[common_snps, common_snps, drop = FALSE]
  w <- weights[common_snps]
  denominator <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(w) %*% ld_gene %*% w))
  
  if (!is.finite(denominator) || denominator == 0){
    message(sprintf(" [skip] %s: degenerate weight normalization.", gene))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  z_snps <- z_sub[match(common_snps, id), z]
  
  list(
    common_snps = common_snps,
    gene_z = sum(w *z_snps) / denominator,
    gene_ld_col = as.vector(ld_gene %*% w) / denominator
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: helper-assemble-joint-inputs

#' Assemble SNP and gene signals for joint fine-mapping
#'
#' @param gene_entries Named list of outputs from build_gene_entry().
#' @param ld_snps SNP correlation matrix for the locus.
#' @param z_sub GWAS z-scores for the selected trait.
#' @return A list with joint z-scores, joint correlation matrix,
#'   and a SNP/Gene type label for each entry.
assemble_joint_inputs <- function(gene_entries, ld_snps, z_sub){
  all_snps <- Reduce(
    union,
    lapply(gene_entries, function(entry) entry$common_snps)
  )
  gene_names <- names(gene_entries)
  
  base_ld <- ld_snps[all_snps, all_snps, drop = FALSE]
  base_z <- z_sub[match(all_snps, id), z]
  names(base_z) <- all_snps
  
  n_snps <- length(all_snps)
  n_genes <- length(gene_names)
  
  ld_joint <- rbind(
    cbind(base_ld, matrix(0, n_snps, n_genes)),
    cbind(matrix(0, n_genes, n_snps), diag(n_genes))
  )
  rownames(ld_joint) <- colnames(ld_joint) <- c(all_snps, gene_names)
  
  for (gene in gene_names){
    entry <- gene_entries[[gene]]
    correlations <- setNames(rep(0, n_snps), all_snps)
    correlations[entry$common_snps] <- entry$gene_ld_col
    
    ld_joint[all_snps, gene] <- correlations
    ld_joint[gene, all_snps] <- correlations
  }
  
  gene_z <- vapply(
    gene_entries, 
    function(entry) entry$gene_z, 
    numeric(1)
  )
  z_joint <- c(base_z, gene_z)
  
  type <- setNames(
    c(rep("SNP", n_snps), rep("Gene", n_genes)),
    names(z_joint)
  )
  
  list(z = z_joint, R = ld_joint, type = type)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: helper-make-locus-prior-weights

#' Assign optional SNP and gene group prior weights
#'
#' @param type Named vector labeling each entry SNP or Gene.
#' @param group_prior_weights NULL for SuSiE's default uniform prior,
#'   or a named vector with SNP and Gene weights.
#' @return NULL or one prior weight per entry.
make_locus_prior_weights <- function(type, group_prior_weights = NULL){
  if (is.null(group_prior_weights)){
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if (!all(c("SNP", "Gene") %in% names(group_prior_weights))){
    stop("group_prior_weights must have SNP and Gene entries.")
  }
  
  weights <- ifelse(
    type == "Gene",
    group_prior_weights["Gene"],
    group_prior_weights["SNP"]
  )
  setNames(as.numeric(weights), names(type))
}
```

### 5.2 Define the helper `run_ctwas_locus_region`

```{r}
#| label: helper-run-ctwas-locus-region 

#' Fine-map one behavioral trait at one candidate locus
#'
#' Coordinate SNP selection, sample alignment, gene signal construction,
#' and a joint SuSiE RSS fit.
#'
#' @param target_trait Behavioral trait name in gwas_zscore.
#' @param target_genes Character vector of candidate gene IDs.
#' @param chr Chromosome identifier.
#' @param start_pos,end_pos Inclusive genomic window boundaries.
#' @param gwas_zscore Prepared GWAS table from prep_gemma_zscores().
#' @param geno_dt Genotype data.table.
#' @param expr_dt Expression data.table.
#' @param n_gwas_samples GWAS sample size passed to susie_rss().
#' @param group_prior_weights NULL for uniform priors, or a named
#'   vector containing SNP and Gene weights.
#' @return A data.table of SNP and gene PIPs, ordered from highest
#'   to lowest; NULL if the locus cannot be analyzed.
run_ctwas_locus_region <- function(
    target_trait,
    target_genes,
    chr,
    start_pos,
    end_pos,
    gwas_zscore,
    geno_dt,
    expr_dt,
    n_gwas_samples = 500,
    group_prior_weights = NULL
){
  message(
    sprintf(
      "--> Fine-mapping Chr %s:%s-%s for %s",
      chr,
      start_pos,
      end_pos,
      paste(target_genes, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
  
  z_sub <- gwas_zscore[Trait == target_trait]
  locus_geno <- select_locus_genotypes(
    geno_dt, chr, start_pos, end_pos
  )
  
  if (nrow(locus_geno) < 2) {
    message("Not enough SNPs in the physical window.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  aligned <- align_locus_samples(locus_geno, geno_dt, expr_dt)
  if (is.null(aligned)) return(NULL)
  
  ld_snps <- cor(aligned$X, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  gene_entries <- lapply(
    target_genes,
    build_gene_entry,
    expr_dt = expr_dt,
    aligned = aligned,
    ld_snps = ld_snps,
    z_sub = z_sub
  )
  names(gene_entries) <- target_genes
  gene_entries <- Filter(Negate(is.null), gene_entries)
  
  if (length(gene_entries) == 0) {
    message("No candidate gene produced a suitable usable weight model.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  joint <- assemble_joint_inputs(gene_entries, ld_snps, z_sub)
  priors <- make_locus_prior_weights(
    joint$type, group_prior_weights
  )
  
  fit <- susieR::susie_rss(
    z = joint$z,
    R = joint$R,
    n = n_gwas_samples,
    L = min(5, length(joint$z)),
    prior_weights = priors,
    check_R = FALSE
  )
  
  results <- data.table(
    Locus_Chr = chr,
    Locus_Start = start_pos,
    Locus_End = end_pos,
    Trait = target_trait,
    ID = names(joint$z),
    Type = joint$type[names(joint$z)],
    PIP = fit$pip
  )
  
  results[order(-PIP)]
}
```

### 5.3 Check the function on one locus

```{r}
#| label: check-one-locus

trial_result <- run_ctwas_locus_region(
  target_trait = "X_MIDDLE_FG_2",
  target_genes = "ENSGALG00010024904",  # ALS2CL
  chr = "2",
  start_pos = 3275060,
  end_pos = 3282960,
  gwas_zscore = gwas_zscore,
  geno_dt = geno_dt,
  expr_dt = expr_dt,
  n_gwas_samples = 375,
  group_prior_weights = NULL
)

trial_result
```

**Observation**

The trial run returned PIPs for nine SNPs and one candidate gene in the selected locus. Several SNPs received high PIPs, whereas ALS2CL received a PIP of 0.065. The function therefore produces the expected output structure; these results will be interpreted alongside the remaining loci and the second pass.

## 6. Choose the loci and candidate genes

### 6.1 Identify GWAS regions and candidate genes

Inspect GWAS regions and eQTL evidence

```{r}
#| label: inspect-gwas-regions-candidate

# GWAS SNPs grouped by trait and sweep region
gwas_regions <- gemma_gwas_dt[
  ,
  .(
    gwas_snps = .N,
    start = min(Position),
    end = max(Position),
    host_genes = paste(
      unique(
        na.omit(SNP_HostGeneEnsemblID),
      ),
      collapse = ", "
    )
  ),
  by = .(Trait, Chromosome, PopSweepRegionID)
][
  order(Trait, Chromosome, start)
]

gwas_regions
```

```{r}
#| Label: eqtl-candidates
#| 
# eQTL genes
eqtl_candidates <- eqtl_dt[
  gene %in% expr_dt$ID,
  .(
    gene,
    SNP,
    FDR,
    peak_type,
    sweep_region_ids
  )
]

eqtl_candidates
```

**Observations**

GWAS data produce 57 trait–region combinations. The eQTL check finds four significant genes, that also have expression data: `ENSGALG00010008087`, `ENSGALG00010009173`, `ENSGALG00010011018`, and `ENSGALG00010021786`. All four eQTL entries are labeled *cis*. The table will be narrowed before choosing loci. Several combinations contain only one reported GWAS SNP, so locus selection must also check that enough SNPs are available for fine-mapping.

**Narrow GWAS regions**

```{r}
#| label: narrow-table-for-loci-selection

gwas_regions_narrowed <- gwas_regions[
  PopSweepRegionID %in% eqtl_candidates$sweep_region_ids
  & gwas_snps >= 2,
  .(
    Trait,
    Chromosome,
    PopSweepRegionID,
    gwas_snps,
    start,
    end,
    host_genes
  )
]

gwas_regions_narrowed
```

### 6.2 Define `loci_table`

Four distinct sweep regions were selected. Each has a candidate gene measured in the expression data with cis-eQTL evidence, and the selected trait has at least two reported GWAS SNPs. The fine-mapping function will check whether sufficient variable genotype SNPs also overlap the GWAS results. The following starts and ends are guided by the lab's requested first and last GWAS SNP in the sweep.

```{r}
#| label: define-loci-table

loci_table <- list(
  list(
    trait = "MEANXOTHER_D", chr = "1",
    start = 15702813, end = 15709825,
    genes = c("ENSGALG00010008087"), n = 375
  ),
  list(
    trait = "LN_MEANXSAME_A", chr = "1",
    start = 76741609, end = 76750239,
    genes = c("ENSGALG00010021786"), n = 375
  ),
  list(
    trait = "MEANXOTHER_D", chr = "4",
    start = 75520158, end = 75528418,
    genes = c("ENSGALG00010011018"), n = 375
  ),
  list(
    trait = "MEANXOTHER_D", chr = "4",
    start = 78060499, end = 78068142,
    genes = c("ENSGALG00010009173"), n = 375
  )
)

data.table::rbindlist(lapply(loci_table, as.data.table))
```

### 6.3 Check phenotype availability for selected traits

```{r}
#| label: inspect-trait-sample-counts

traits_to_check <- unique(c(
  "X_MIDDLE_FG_2",
  vapply(loci_table, `[[`, character(1), "trait")
))

data.table::rbindlist(lapply(traits_to_check, function(trait) {
  data.table(
    Trait = trait,
    nonmissing_phenotypes_with_genotypes = sum(
      pheno_dt$ID %in% genotype_samples &
        !is.na(pheno_dt[[trait]])
    )
  )
}))
```

**Observations**

Although genotype and expression data are available for 375 matching individuals, only 59, 22, and 23 of them have recorded values for the three traits checked here. These counts do not establish the exact sample sizes used in the original GEMMA analyses. Therefore, the `n = 375` values specified using the lab's genotype-count instruction are working assumptions, and the resulting PIPs is to be interpreted with that limitation.

## 7. Pass 1 — Fine-map with uniform priors

Running every locus once, with `group_prior_weights = NULL`

```{r}
#| label: run-pass1-uniform-priors

pass1_by_locus <- lapply(seq_along(loci_table), function(i) {
  locus <- loci_table[[i]]
  
  run_ctwas_locus_region(
    target_trait = locus$trait,
    target_genes = locus$genes,
    chr = locus$chr,
    start_pos = locus$start,
    end_pos = locus$end,
    gwas_zscore = gwas_zscore,
    geno_dt = geno_dt,
    expr_dt = expr_dt,
    n_gwas_samples = locus$n,
    group_prior_weights = NULL
  )
})

failed_loci <- which(
  vapply(pass1_by_locus, is.null, logical(1))
)

if (length(failed_loci) > 0) {
  stop(
    "No results for loci_table entries: ",
    paste(failed_loci, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

pass1_results <- data.table::rbindlist(pass1_by_locus)
```

```{r}
#| label: inspect-pass1-results

pass1_results[
  ,
  .(
    SNPs = sum(Type == "SNP"),
    Genes = sum(Type == "Gene"),
    top_ID = ID[which.max(PIP)],
    top_Type = Type[which.max(PIP)],
    top_PIP = max(PIP)
  ),
  by = .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End)
]

pass1_results[
  Type == "Gene",
  .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End, ID, PIP)
]
```

**Observations**

Pass 1 produced SNP and gene PIPs for all four selected loci using uniform priors. A gene had the highest PIP in two loci, although neither gene PIP exceeded 0.37. A SNP had the highest PIP in the other two loci, with PIPs of approximately 0.993 and 1.000. These are preliminary results because the GWAS sample size supplied to the model remains unverified.

## 8. Estimate empirical group priors from pass 1

```{r}
#| label: estimate-empirical-group-priors

empirical_prior <- pass1_results[
  ,
  .(
    entries = .N,
    mean_PIP = mean(PIP)
  ),
  by = Type
]

stopifnot(setequal(empirical_prior$Type, c("SNP", "Gene")))

group_prior_weights <- setNames(
  empirical_prior$mean_PIP,
  empirical_prior$Type
)

# Keep a group with a zero or missing mean PIP eligible in pass 2.
group_prior_weights[
  !is.finite(group_prior_weights) | group_prior_weights <= 0
] <- 0.01

empirical_prior
group_prior_weights
```

**Observations**

Across the four pass 1 loci, the mean PIP was 0.212 for the four gene entries and 0.196 for the 45 SNP entries. These values provide slightly higher per-entry weight for genes in pass 2. Because they were estimated from only four selected loci, they are exploratory weights rather than independently calibrated cTWAS priors.

## 9. Pass 2 — Fine-map with calibrated priors

```{r}
#| label: run-pass2-calibrated-priors

pass2_by_locus <- lapply(seq_along(loci_table), function(i) {
  locus <- loci_table[[i]]
  
  run_ctwas_locus_region(
    target_trait = locus$trait,
    target_genes = locus$genes,
    chr = locus$chr,
    start_pos = locus$start,
    end_pos = locus$end,
    gwas_zscore = gwas_zscore,
    geno_dt = geno_dt,
    expr_dt = expr_dt,
    n_gwas_samples = locus$n,
    group_prior_weights = group_prior_weights
  )
})

failed_loci <- which(vapply(pass2_by_locus, is.null, logical(1)))

if (length(failed_loci) > 0) {
  stop(
    "No pass 2 results for loci_table entries: ",
    paste(failed_loci, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

pass2_results <- data.table::rbindlist(pass2_by_locus)
```

```{r}
#| label: inspect-pass2-results

pass2_results[
  ,
  .(
    SNPs = sum(Type == "SNP"),
    Genes = sum(Type == "Gene"),
    top_ID = ID[which.max(PIP)],
    top_Type = Type[which.max(PIP)],
    top_PIP = max(PIP)
  ),
  by = .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End)
]

pass2_results[
  Type == "Gene",
  .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End, ID, PIP)
]
```

**Observations**

Pass 2 completed for all four selected loci using the group weights estimated in Section 8. Each locus retained one candidate gene. A gene had the highest PIP in two loci, while a SNP had the highest PIP in the other two. These PIPs remain preliminary because the GWAS sample size used in the analysis has not been verified.

## 10. Compare pass 1 and pass 2

### 10.1 PIP comparison table

```{r}
#| label: compare-pass-pips

entry_cols <- c(
  "Trait", "Locus_Chr", "Locus_Start", "Locus_End", "Type", "ID"
)

# Check that each entry appears once in each pass.
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(pass1_results[, ..entry_cols]),
  !anyDuplicated(pass2_results[, ..entry_cols])
)

pip_comparison <- merge(
  pass1_results[, c(entry_cols, "PIP"), with = FALSE],
  pass2_results[, c(entry_cols, "PIP"), with = FALSE],
  by = entry_cols,
  suffixes = c("_pass1", "_pass2")
)

# A missing match would make this comparison incomplete.
stopifnot(
  nrow(pip_comparison) == nrow(pass1_results),
  nrow(pip_comparison) == nrow(pass2_results)
)

pip_comparison[, delta_PIP := PIP_pass2 - PIP_pass1]

# Entries with the largest absolute changes.
head(
  pip_comparison[order(-abs(delta_PIP))],
  12
)
```

```{r}
#| label: compare-gene-pips

pip_comparison[
  Type == "Gene",
  .(
    Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End, ID,
    PIP_pass1, PIP_pass2, delta_PIP
  )
][order(Locus_Chr, Locus_Start)]
```

### 10.2 Question 1: What changed?

After applying the empirical group weights, the PIP increased for each of the four candidate genes by 0.0061–0.0188. Several SNP PIPs decreased slightly. The leading entry did not change in any of the four loci: ENSGALG00010008087 and ENSGALG00010011018 remained the leading genes in their respective loci, while 1:76750239 and 4:78065006 remained the leading SNPs in theirs. Because the weights were estimated from pass 1 using these same loci, the increases in gene PIP are a consequence of the prior adjustment, not independent evidence for the genes.

## 11. Compare GWAS associations with fine-mapping

### 11.1 Join GEMMA p-values to SNP PIPs

```{r}
#| label: join-gwas-pvalues-snp-pips

gwas_for_comparison <- gemma_gwas_dt[
  ,
  .(
    Trait,
    ID = SNP_ID,
    Chromosome = as.character(Chromosome),
    Position,
    PvalueLRT
  )
]

snp_comparison <- merge(
  pass2_results[
    Type == "SNP",
    .(
      Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End,
      ID, PIP_pass2 = PIP
    )
  ],
  gwas_for_comparison,
  by = c("Trait", "ID"),
  all.x = TRUE
)

# Confirm that all 45 fine-mapped SNPs found their GWAS record
# and that each record belongs to the expected locus.
stopifnot(
  nrow(snp_comparison) == sum(pass2_results$Type == "SNP"),
  !anyNA(snp_comparison$PvalueLRT),
  all(snp_comparison$Chromosome == snp_comparison$Locus_Chr),
  all(snp_comparison$Position >= snp_comparison$Locus_Start),
  all(snp_comparison$Position <= snp_comparison$Locus_End)
)

snp_comparison[
  ,
  `:=`(
    GWAS_rank = data.table::frank(PvalueLRT, ties.method = "min"),
    PIP_rank = data.table::frank(-PIP_pass2, ties.method = "min")
  ),
  by = .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End)
]

# Show the SNP leading by either measure in each locus.
snp_comparison[
  GWAS_rank == 1 | PIP_rank == 1,
  .(
    Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, ID,
    PvalueLRT, GWAS_rank, PIP_pass2, PIP_rank
  )
][order(Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, GWAS_rank, PIP_rank)]
```

### 11.2 Question 2: Do the rankings agree?

The SNP with the smallest GEMMA p-value also had the highest pass 2 SNP PIP in two of the four loci. The rankings differed in both chromosome 4 loci. Most strikingly, 4:78065006 had the highest SNP PIP in its locus (displayed as 1.0000), although it ranked fourth by GWAS p-value. Thus, strong individual GWAS association did not consistently identify the SNP receiving the strongest fine-mapping support. GEMMA tests SNP associations individually, whereas fine-mapping considers the SNPs together with the candidate gene and their correlation structure.

## 12. Examine gene-level support

### 12.1 Compare gene and SNP PIPs within loci

```{r}
#| label: compare-gene-and-snp-support

gene_support <- pass2_results[
  Type == "Gene",
  .(gene_ID = ID, gene_PIP = PIP),
  by = .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End)
]

snp_support <- pass2_results[
  Type == "SNP",
  .(
    top_SNP = ID[which.max(PIP)],
    top_SNP_PIP = max(PIP)
  ),
  by = .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End)
]

locus_support <- merge(
  gene_support,
  snp_support,
  by = c("Trait", "Locus_Chr", "Locus_Start", "Locus_End")
)

locus_support[
  ,
  .(
    Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start,
    gene_ID, gene_PIP, top_SNP, top_SNP_PIP,
    suggestive_gene_without_suggestive_SNP =
      gene_PIP > 0.25 & top_SNP_PIP <= 0.25
  )
][order(Locus_Chr, Locus_Start)]
```

### 12.2 Question 3: Are there examples where a gene is significant in a given region but no SNPs are reliably flagged as causal? If so, what does this mean?

No gene reached the walkthrough’s PIP \> 0.75 threshold for “significant” support. However, ENSGALG00010008087 and ENSGALG00010011018 each had a suggestive gene PIP (\> 0.25) without any SNP in its locus reaching 0.25. This suggests that the gene expression signal may capture support that is not assigned strongly to any individual SNP. It does not establish that either gene is causal: the result depends on the fine-mapping model, its priors, and the GWAS sample size used.

## 13. Annotate selected variants with VEP

### 13.1 Select high- and low-PIP SNPs

```{r}
#| label: select-snps-for-vep

vep_candidates <- pass2_results[
  Type == "SNP",
  {
    selected <- c(which.max(PIP), which.min(PIP))
    .(
      selection = c("Highest SNP PIP", "Lowest SNP PIP"),
      ID = ID[selected],
      PIP = PIP[selected]
    )
  },
  by = .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End)
]

vep_candidates[
  order(Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, -PIP)
]
```

**Observations**

“Highest” and “lowest” refer to the SNP PIPs within each locus. Only two selected SNPs exceed the walkthrough’s 0.75 threshold: 1:76750239 (PIP 0.9930) in the chromosome 1 locus starting at 76,741,609, and 4:78065006 (PIP displayed as 1.0000) in the chromosome 4 locus starting at 78,060,499.

### 13.2 Verify alleles and genome assembly

```{r}
#| label: inspect-vep-candidate-alleles

geno_letters_dt <- data.table::fread(
  "../data/student_trial_genotypes_letters.txt"
)

# Identify candidates without allele calls.
setdiff(vep_candidates$ID, geno_letters_dt$SNP)
# Expected: "4:78062977"

# Re-select the high- and low-PIP SNPs among variants
# represented in the genotype letters file.
vep_candidates <- pass2_results[
  Type == "SNP" & ID %in% geno_letters_dt$SNP,
  {
    selected <- c(which.max(PIP), which.min(PIP))
    .(
      selection = c("Highest SNP PIP", "Lowest SNP PIP"),
      ID = ID[selected],
      PIP = PIP[selected]
    )
  },
  by = .(Trait, Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, Locus_End)
]

stopifnot(
  nrow(vep_candidates) == 8L,
  all(vep_candidates$ID %in% geno_letters_dt$SNP)
)

allele_summary <- data.table::rbindlist(
  lapply(vep_candidates$ID, function(snp) {
    calls <- unlist(
      geno_letters_dt[
        SNP == snp,
        setdiff(names(geno_letters_dt), "SNP"),
        with = FALSE
      ],
      use.names = FALSE
    )
    
    alleles <- sort(unique(unlist(
      strsplit(calls[!is.na(calls)], "|", fixed = TRUE)
    )))
    
    data.table::data.table(
      ID = snp,
      observed_alleles = paste(alleles, collapse = "/"),
      n_observed_alleles = length(alleles)
    )
  })
)

vep_alleles <- merge(
  vep_candidates,
  allele_summary,
  by = "ID",
  all.x = TRUE
)

vep_alleles[
  order(Locus_Chr, Locus_Start, -PIP),
  .(ID, selection, PIP, observed_alleles, n_observed_alleles)
]
```

**Observations**

The genotype letters file contains allele calls for all eight final VEP candidates. Each has two observed bases. The lowest-PIP SNP originally selected in the locus starting at chromosome 4 position 78,060,499 was absent from that file, so 4:78060950 was selected as the lowest-PIP SNP with available allele calls.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-vep-position-check

vep_alleles[
  , c("Chromosome", "Position") := data.table::tstrsplit(
    ID, ":", fixed = TRUE
  )
]
vep_alleles[, Position := as.integer(Position)]

vep_alleles[
  order(Chromosome, Position),
  .(ID, Chromosome, Position, selection, PIP, observed_alleles)
]
```

Eight SNPs were selected for VEP annotation: the highest- and lowest-PIP SNP from each of four loci. Two exceeded the walkthrough’s PIP threshold of 0.75, while six were below it, allowing comparison of variants with strong and weaker fine-mapping support.\
